investigacion.base:
Check if filed already this week.As of October 20, 2026, I found no report that the retrial petition has actually reached the Suwon High Court. All the coverage, dated October 14, describes a plan to file "next week," meaning October 19–23. I also couldn't pull up Yonhap's English search page or the Metaculus FAQ directly, so I can't say what those resolution sources show right now.

**Latest news (Oct 13–14, 2026)**
- **Oct 13:** Lee's five lawyers met for about two hours. They agreed to pursue only a retrial and to drop parole, special pardon and other steps.  They then visited him at the Suwon Detention Center, explained the decision and got his agreement. 
- **Oct 14:** The lawyers' official statement said the retrial request would be filed "within this month."  Several outlets reported they planned to submit it to the Suwon High Court next week. 
- **What the petition targets:** the appeals-court ruling that the Supreme Court made final. Under criminal procedure law, a retrial goes to the court that issued the original ruling, so it goes to the Suwon High Court, which handled the second trial.  That matches the question's requirement: it's the 7-year-8-month conviction, not the separate third-party bribery case.
- **Main argument:** a level-2 classified National Intelligence Service (NIS) document, which the defence says counts as newly discovered evidence.  In April, at the parliamentary investigation into allegedly fabricated indictments, NIS Director Lee Jong-seok said the Suwon District Prosecutors' Office took only 13 of 66 NIS reports on the remittances. 
- **How and when it will be filed:** the lawyers are considering filing by mail, and the exact date could change depending on their review.  In the days after Oct 14, they planned to meet Lee again to work out the specific grounds. 
- **Background:** in early October there was controversy over reports that Lee wanted early release and resented President Lee Jae-myung. He denied ever attacking the president.  The Kookmin Ilbo also reported plans to seek relief from the UN Human Rights Committee. 

**Status quo and timing**
- Target window: Oct 19–23. Hard deadline the lawyers set themselves: end of October, which matches the Oct 31 cutoff.
- Risks:
  - The petition is filed late, for example to strengthen the grounds.
  - A mailed petition arrives after Oct 31. Only actual receipt by the court counts, and only by that date.
- No court events are scheduled. Filing is entirely up to the defence.

**Base rates and context**
- Lawyers in high-profile Korean cases usually file publicly announced petitions on or close to the stated date, though slips of a week or two do happen.
- Legal experts are sceptical that a retrial will be granted or the conviction overturned, because retrials are allowed only in very exceptional cases.  That affects the outcome of the petition, not whether it gets filed.

**Current read:** this would resolve NO today, since there's no confirmed filing. But the lawyers have firmly and publicly committed to filing by the end of October, with about 11 days left. Look for "재심청구서 접수" (petition received) reports from Yonhap, News1 or Newsis this week. I didn't find any prediction-market prices for this question.

criterios: This question resolves YES if, at any point through October 31, 2026 (Korea Standard Time, UTC+9), the legal team of Lee Hwa-young (이화영), former Gyeonggi Province Vice Governor for Peace, has formally submitted (filed) a petition for retrial (재심청구서) to the Suwon High Court (수원고법) in the Ssangbangwool (쌍방울) illegal North Korea remittance case for which the Supreme Court finalized his seven-year-eight-month prison sentence in June 2025. Filing by any means accepted by the court (including submission by mail that has been received by the court) counts. The question resolves based on reporting from [Yonhap News](https://en.yna.co.kr/search/index?query=Lee+Hwa-young) or other [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). It resolves NO if no such petition has been received by the Suwon High Court as of that date.
letra_pequena: A petition for retrial concerning a different case (for example, the separate third-party bribery remittance case) does not count; only a petition targeting the finalized conviction for which the seven-year-eight-month sentence was imposed counts. A publicly stated intention or announcement of plans to file, without the petition actually having been received by the court, does not count. If the court's receipt of a mailed petition is reported after October 31, 2026 but establishes that receipt occurred on or before October 31, 2026 (KST), the question resolves YES.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 11 days, through October 31 in Korea.

(b) **Status quo:** No qualifying petition has been reported as received by the Suwon High Court. If nothing changes, the answer is No.

(c) **Reference class:** When a legal team publicly commits to an imminent filing and names a deadline, I would usually expect it to file. As a rough judgment—not a measured base rate—I would put comparable filings within the stated window at around 75–85%.

(d) **No scenario:** The lawyers take longer to prepare the petition, or mail it too late for the court to receive it by October 31.

(e) **Yes scenario:** They complete their review and the Suwon High Court receives the petition next week or by month-end.

(f) **Technicality:** Announcing or mailing a petition is insufficient; the court must **receive** a petition targeting this specific finalized conviction by the deadline.

Probability: 80%

(a) **Time left:** About 11 days, through October 31, 2026, Korea time.

(b) **Status quo:** NO. As of October 20, there is no confirmed filing.

(c) **Reference class:** When a represented legal team publicly announces a specific court filing for the next week or two, I would expect it to follow through roughly 75–85% of the time. That is a judgmental base rate, not a measured statistic.

(d) **NO scenario:** The lawyers delay to develop the new-evidence argument, or mail the petition too late for the court to receive it by October 31.

(e) **YES scenario:** They complete the petition and the Suwon High Court receives it this week or next, as announced.

(f) **Decisive technicality:** An announcement—or a petition merely put in the mail—does not count. The court must receive a petition targeting the finalized seven-year-eight-month conviction by the cutoff.

The team’s explicit commitment and near-term plan make filing more likely than not, but the unfixed date and possible mail delay leave meaningful risk.

Probability: 83%

(a) About 11 days remain, until October 31, 2026 (KST). Confirmation of receipt would likely be reported within a few days of filing.

(b) If nothing changed, the question resolves NO. As of October 16 the Suwon High Court had received no petition, and I found no report of a filing through October 20.

(c) The reference class is defence teams in high-profile Korean criminal cases that publicly announce a retrial petition with a stated near-term deadline. They usually file within the announced window or shortly after. Slips of one to three weeks are fairly common when counsel want more time to build the "new evidence" grounds. My rough base rate for filing by a self-set month-end deadline, given an announcement about two weeks earlier, is about 65–80%.

(d) A NO scenario: the lawyers decide they need more time to secure or characterize the classified NIS level-2 document. That document may be hard to access or attach, and they may first need to request it formally. Further meetings with Lee to refine the grounds also push things back. The filing slips into November. Or a petition mailed at the very end of October is received after the 31st.

(e) A YES scenario: the team files during the week of October 19–23 or the following week, as announced. It files by mail or in person, and Yonhap, News1 or Newsis report "재심청구서 접수" (petition received) at the Suwon High Court before October 31.

(f) Technicalities in the resolution criteria:
- Only actual receipt by the Suwon High Court counts. Mailing alone does not, so a late-October postmark arriving in November would resolve NO.
- October 31, 2026 is a Saturday, so effectively the last day for receipt is Friday, October 30.
- The petition must target the 7-year-8-month conviction, not the third-party bribery case.

**Overall:** The team has firmly and publicly committed to filing, dropped the parole option and left retrial as its only route, so it is strongly motivated to act. Against that, its strategy has already shifted once this month, the "next week" date was explicitly hedged, and the classified-document basis may take extra preparation.

Probability: 70%
